title: Looper, MessageQueue, Handler, and Frame Starvation Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies looper, messagequeue, handler, and frame starvation?
options: Keep main dispatch bounded and move appropriate work to owned execution while treating coroutine resumption as real queue work.
questions.answer: Keep main dispatch bounded and move appropriate work to owned execution while treating coroutine resumption as real queue work.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: A coroutine launched on Dispatchers.Main automatically moves blocking work off the UI thread.
questions.explanation: Wrapping blocking work in launch on Dispatchers.Main keeps the blocking call on the UI thread even though the code uses a coroutine.

questions.answer: It enqueues work onto the MessageQueue associated with its Looper and therefore onto that Looper thread.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
